facts.fact: Ecofin Agency reports that Nigeria's space agency NASRDA launched CropWatch in 2024, a crop monitoring system that uses satellite data.

On 17 July 2026 a Nigerian government delegation signed an MoU with OCP Africa and Ground Truth Analytics to launch the National Agro-Productivity System, a satellite and AI crop monitoring platform using images updated every five days, to start with a pilot in one state.

systems.owner: Nigerian government with OCP Africa and Ground Truth Analytics

NGA.note: The document states nothing on AI rules or an authority over AI harms.
The only AI system named is a sector (agriculture) platform, which is not general administration.

facts.fact: Nigeria signed an MoU on 17 July 2026 to launch NAPS, an agricultural monitoring platform whose AI algorithms identify farmland and crops from satellite images, to be deployed gradually starting with a one-state pilot.

systems.owner: Nigerian government with OCP Africa and Ground Truth Analytics

NGA.note: The document names no AI model, dataset or AI computing built or hosted in Nigeria.
Nothing on the central bank or payments.
Nothing on consumer protection in digital finance.

facts.fact: Nigeria's government said it will host all data generated by the NAPS agricultural monitoring platform on domestic servers to preserve national data sovereignty.

NGA.note: Nothing on government payments to people.
